paragraphs: Overall credibility check result for this report is: not passed. Results for step s_combo1 (static, combo1) must therefore not be described as converged or reliable.

Reaction balance passed, so the applied load is balanced by the support reactions. The maximum displacement is {{s_combo1.u_max_mm}}, and it is stable across the three mesh levels ({{s_combo1.conv3.level0}}, {{s_combo1.conv3.level1}}, {{s_combo1.conv3.level2}}), so the displacement check passed.

The maximum von Mises stress (excluding the constrained faces) is {{s_combo1.vm_max_mpa}}. It did not converge: it rises with refinement from {{s_combo1.conv2.level0}} to {{s_combo1.conv2.level1}} and then {{s_combo1.conv2.level2}}. This points to a suspected stress singularity, such as a sharp corner or point load. This stress cannot be used as a design basis. Comparison with the yield strength of {{s_combo1.strength_mpa}} is not meaningful for this value.

The mesh quality check is unknown. Second-order elements on curved surfaces were too distorted after upgrading, so straight-edge second-order elements were used, with the curved surfaces approximated by chords. Stress near curved surfaces may deviate noticeably.
No safety factor is given, because the credibility checks did not pass.

Limitations: linear elastic, small deformation; no contact; residual stress and surface hardening are not considered. Stresses near constrained and loaded faces come from idealized boundary conditions and were excluded from the maximum-stress evaluation. Stress at sharp corners grows with mesh refinement (theoretical singularity) and should not be used directly for design.
suggestions: Locate the position of the maximum von Mises stress and have an engineer check whether it lies at a sharp corner or point load.
If the corner is real, model it with an actual fillet radius, or replace the point load with a distributed load, then rerun the mesh convergence study.
Refine the mesh on curved surfaces so that there are several element layers across them, and then repeat the mesh quality check.
Evaluate stress at the suspected singularity using a hot-spot or structural-stress method, or a local submodel with realistic geometry, instead of the raw peak value.
Supply the actual fillet and load-application details to the analyst so that a safety factor can be considered after all credibility checks pass.
